name: Data Legion
summary: Person and company enrichment and SQL-style search over 188M+ person and 71M+ company profiles, with optional contact data.

api_key.description: A Data Legion API key (dashboard, after sign-up). Sent in the API-Key header.

notes: Prepaid credits: 1 credit = 1 record returned; the price per credit depends on the product bought (base or premium, with or without contact data). Credits-Used and Credits-Remaining response headers report the charge.
Rate limits per account: enrichment 100/min, search and discover 10/min (search 5/min on a free trial); 429 carries Retry-After.
Free-trial person results redact contact data until a card is verified.
Search takes SQL without LIMIT/OFFSET: use limit, offset (max 10000) and cursor. A 408 timeout is not charged.
Bulk enrichment and data-issue reports are documented but not in this entry.

endpoints.name: Enrich a person
endpoints.summary: Best matching person profile (work history, education, skills, socials; contact data on contact plans) from an identifier, or a name plus context.

social_url.description: LinkedIn, X, GitHub or Facebook profile URL.

email_hash.description: SHA-256, SHA-1 or MD5 of the normalized email.

first_name.description: First name; with last_name needs a context field.

full_name.description: Full name of two or more words, instead of first and last.

company.description: Company name, website or social URL (context).

school.description: School name, website or social URL (context).

birth_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY; context or a narrowing qualifier.

required_fields.description: Fields a match must have, else it is dropped and not billed, e.g. work_email or emails.type:personal.

titlecase.description: Title-case text fields (names, titles, companies, locations).

include_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return; all if omitted.

exclude_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to leave out, applied after include_fields.

notes: A read over POST. Needs one primary identifier (email, phone, social_url, linkedin_id, legion_id, email_hash) or a first and last name plus a context field; otherwise 400.
1 credit per record returned; 404 when nothing matches.

endpoints.name: Search people with SQL
endpoints.summary: People matching a SQL WHERE clause over 100+ profile columns, with an exact or estimated total.

query.description: SQL 'SELECT * FROM people WHERE ...' without LIMIT/OFFSET (an Elasticsearch-style query object is also accepted).
query.example: SELECT * FROM people WHERE company_name ILIKE '%google%' AND state = 'california'

offset.description: Results to skip, 0-10000; use cursor beyond.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous page; send without offset and with the same query.

titlecase.description: Title-case text fields (names, titles, companies, locations).

include_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return; all if omitted.

exclude_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to leave out, applied after include_fields.

notes: A read over POST. 1 credit per record returned; total (with the Total-Count-Status header) gives the match count, so limit 1 sizes a market cheaply.
10 requests a minute (5 on a free trial).

endpoints.name: Discover people in plain English
endpoints.summary: People matching a natural-language description; the SQL it generated comes back as generated_query.

query.example: VPs of Engineering at fintech companies in New York

titlecase.description: Title-case text fields (names, titles, companies, locations).

include_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return; all if omitted.

exclude_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to leave out, applied after include_fields.

notes: A read over POST. Beta and enterprise-only (not on self-serve plans).

endpoints.name: Enrich a company
endpoints.summary: Best matching company profile (firmographics, locations, workforce data) by domain, name, LinkedIn id, social URL, ticker or Legion id.

social_url.description: LinkedIn, Facebook, Crunchbase, X or GitHub company URL.

industry.description: Narrows a name match, e.g. software development.

required_fields.description: Fields a match must have, else it is dropped and not billed.

titlecase.description: Title-case text fields (names, titles, companies, locations).

include_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return; all if omitted.

exclude_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to leave out, applied after include_fields.

notes: A read over POST. Needs at least one identifier; industry alone is not enough. 1 credit per record returned.

endpoints.name: Search companies with SQL
endpoints.summary: Companies matching a SQL WHERE clause over 50+ firmographic and workforce columns.

query.description: SQL 'SELECT * FROM companies WHERE ...' without LIMIT/OFFSET (an Elasticsearch-style query object is also accepted).
query.example: SELECT * FROM companies WHERE industry ILIKE '%software%' AND legion_employee_count > 100

offset.description: Results to skip, 0-10000; use cursor beyond.

cursor.description: next_cursor of the previous page; send without offset and with the same query.

titlecase.description: Title-case text fields (names, titles, companies, locations).

include_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return; all if omitted.

exclude_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to leave out, applied after include_fields.

notes: A read over POST. 1 credit per record returned. An industry value no record holds returns an empty page free, with a Search-Warning header.

endpoints.name: Discover companies in plain English
endpoints.summary: Companies matching a natural-language description, with the generated SQL.

query.example: AI startups in San Francisco with over 50 employees

titlecase.description: Title-case text fields (names, titles, companies, locations).

include_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return; all if omitted.

exclude_fields.description: Comma-separated fields to leave out, applied after include_fields.

notes: A read over POST. Beta and enterprise-only.

endpoints.summary: Format checks and suggestions for person or company fields before an enrich or search call.
notes: A read over POST. 100 requests a minute.
